title: Split with a Dog 2027: Beaches, Ferries, Rules & Costs
metaDescription: Split with a dog: official dog beaches, ferry and catamaran rules, hotel pet fees, summer heat, vet basics and EU pet passport rules. Clear verdict inside.
content:
## Are Dogs Allowed in Split?

Yes. Split has no general ban on dogs in public spaces. Dogs must be on a leash, owners must clean up after them, and restricted breeds need a muzzle under Croatian rules. The practical limits are heat, a short list of official dog beaches and the transport rules for ferries.

## Dog Beaches in Split (Plaža za Pse)

### Duilovo Dog Beach
Duilovo is the city's first purpose-built dog beach and the only one signed as an official "plaža za pse". It lies on the eastern side of the city, about 4 km from the old town, and is reachable by bus, on foot or by car. The beach is a small semicircle of smooth pebbles with a shallow entrance. Reports mention showers, changing cabins and small shade tents. Reviews also note there is no natural shade, a construction site next door and no bar. Where sunbeds and drinks are offered, expect roughly €20 per sunbed and about €6 per drink. Off-leash dogs are common and not every dog is friendly, so check the mood before unclipping.

### Kašjuni and Other Marjan Coves
Kašjuni, on the south side of the Marjan peninsula about 5 km from Riva, has a section designated for dogs. It has no facilities, so bring water and shade. Kaštelet, also on Marjan, is a quieter rocky spot. Trstenik and Žnjan have signed dog sections, and Stobreč to the east also has a dog-friendly beach. Marjan's rock entries suit early-morning swims.

### Dogs on Other Beaches
Outside the designated areas, dogs are not allowed on most managed beaches. Bačvice, the main city beach, restricts pets in summer. Look for the pictogram at the beach entrance. Rocky, unmanaged coves are tolerated by many locals but are not official.

## Old Town, Restaurants and Parks

Dogs on a leash can walk through Diocletian's Palace and along the Riva at any hour. The polished limestone gets very hot in July and August, so walk in the early morning or after 19:00. Terraces and outdoor seating at cafés and konobas usually accept dogs. Indoor dining is at the owner's discretion, and many places refuse dogs inside. Ask before sitting down. Marjan Forest Park is the best walking area, with shaded trails and the dog-friendly café at the first viewpoint (Vidilica).

An opinion worth following: skip the Riva at midday with a dog. The stone and the crowds make it miserable for the animal, and Marjan's shaded paths are better at any hour.

## National Parks and Day Trips

Croatian national parks generally allow dogs on a leash, but not in swimming zones. Krka (about 85 km from Split) accepts leashed dogs on trails. Dogs are not allowed on Visovac Island, and a muzzle is required on park boats and shuttle buses. Plitvice Lakes also admits leashed dogs, but swimming is banned there.

## Ferries and Catamarans from Split

- **Car ferries (Jadrolinija):** Dogs travel free. Dogs over 8 kg stay on the open deck on a leash and with a muzzle. Small pets under 8 kg ride in a carrier on your lap or under the seat. Split–Supetar (Brač) takes about 50 minutes.
- **Catamarans:** Rules differ by operator (Jadrolinija, Krilo/Kapetan Luka, TP Line). Some accept only small dogs in a closed carrier, and some offer deck boxes for a fee. Confirm before booking, especially for Hvar (about 1 hr). Larger dogs are much easier on the car ferry to Stari Grad.
- **International (Ancona–Split):** Pets are free and may stay in a cabin, but not in lounges. Book a pet-friendly cabin.

Carry a vaccination certificate and a muzzle on every crossing.

## Accommodation: What a Dog Costs

Pet fees in Split typically run €10–20 per night at hotels and apartments, and some charge a flat cleaning fee per stay. Many private apartments accept dogs for free or a small deposit. Filter by pets allowed, since listings are often not clear, and ask about size limits. Rooms near Marjan, Žnjan or Bačvice make early walks easy.

## Summer Heat and Best Months

July and August regularly reach 30–35 °C. Pavement can burn paws, and dogs must never stay in a parked car. The best months are May, June, September and October, when the sea is warm, the beaches are quieter and walking is comfortable. April and November are cool but fine for walking. In summer, schedule walks before 9:00 and after 19:00 and carry water.

## Vet Basics

Split has the broadest veterinary coverage in Dalmatia, including clinics used to treating visiting pets. Routine consultations generally cost €30–50. Save an emergency vet number before arrival. Ticks and sandflies are active in warm months, so ask your own vet about tick prevention. Hot-weather heatstroke is the most common problem for visiting dogs.

## EU Pet Passport Rules for Driving In

- **Microchip:** ISO-compliant, implanted before the rabies vaccination.
- **Rabies vaccination:** Valid, and at least 21 days old after the primary vaccination before entry.
- **Documents:** An EU pet passport. Travellers from outside the EU, such as the UK, need an animal health certificate issued within 10 days of entry.
- **Number of pets:** Maximum five per traveller for non-commercial travel.
- **Tapeworm treatment:** Not required for Croatia. It is only needed when re-entering countries such as Ireland, Finland, Malta and Norway.
- **Border:** Carry documents in the car. Croatia is in the Schengen area, but pet document checks can still apply at external borders and on some routes through non-EU countries such as Bosnia (Neum corridor).

## Verdict: How Dog-Friendly Is Split?

Split rates about 3.5 out of 5. Dogs are accepted in the old town, on Marjan and on terraces, and the ferry system carries large dogs free of charge. The weak points are one small official dog beach, limited shade, intense summer heat and inconsistent catamaran rules. It works well for a dog holiday in late spring or early autumn and poorly in August.

faq.question: Is there an official dog beach in Split?
faq.answer: Yes. Duilovo (Plaža za pse) is the city's official dog beach, about 4 km east of the old town. A dog section at Kašjuni on Marjan, plus signed sections at Trstenik and Žnjan, are also used.

faq.question: Are dogs allowed in Diocletian's Palace and the old town?
faq.answer: Yes, on a leash. Avoid midday in summer because the stone gets very hot. Outdoor café seating is usually fine, but indoor access depends on the venue.

faq.question: Can dogs go on the ferry from Split?
faq.answer: Yes. Jadrolinija car ferries carry dogs free of charge. Dogs over 8 kg stay on the open deck, leashed and muzzled. Catamarans differ by operator and may limit dogs to small ones in carriers.

faq.question: What does a dog cost at accommodation in Split?
faq.answer: Typically €10–20 per night at hotels and apartments, sometimes with a cleaning fee. Many private apartments accept dogs for free or a small deposit.

faq.question: What are the EU pet passport rules for driving into Croatia?
faq.answer: The dog needs a microchip, a valid rabies vaccination given at least 21 days earlier, and an EU pet passport or animal health certificate for non-EU travellers. Tapeworm treatment is not required for Croatia.

faq.question: What is the best time to visit Split with a dog?
faq.answer: May, June, September and October. Summer temperatures of 30–35 °C make July and August hard on dogs.

quickAnswer: Split is moderately dog-friendly. Leashed dogs are welcome in the old town, on Marjan and in most outdoor restaurant seating. Official dog beaches are Duilovo and a Kašjuni section. Jadrolinija car ferries carry dogs free on open decks, but catamarans restrict them. Visit in May, June, September or October.
